Aaron Sibarium, writing for The Free Beacon:

Paul Crowley, a cybersecurity researcher at Anthropic, is listed as a manager of Red Means No LLC, which says that its parties are “designed to be spaces to … ignore the ‘nos’ of others.” Participants can use a safe word, “red,” to end an encounter but give “default consent” to “spanking,” “wrestling,” and “light pain” by entering the orgy, according to Red Means No’s website. author: Daring Fireball Department of Commerce
description:
Every to-do list runs forever. Ivy runs for a day. Each morning you turn ideas into a plan. Each evening, whatever’s left is an idea again. Nothing is overdue. Tomorrow starts empty.

I’m Jürgen Schweizer, founder of Semantical. I spent years building a to-do app and never expected to build another. Then I came across the Ivy Lee Method. We built a prototype and couldn’t stop using it.

Beneath the calm: Calendar and Reminders integration, focus sessions, Screen Time shields, and a daily journal. All native: SwiftUI, UIKit, Metal.

Ivy is on iPhone, with Mac to follow. Let me know what you think!

 ★
title: [Sponsor] Ivy: The To-do List That Ends

author: John Gruber
description:
Over the weekend I speculated that Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon and have “made their Irish goodbyes” from the Trump 2.0 administration (including having no representatives on the David Sacks-led PCAST). I learned today that what we Americans call an “Irish goodbye” is called a “French leave” in the U.K., and “leaving the English way” in France. The rest of Europe is split between those two, but only Americans and Canadians call it an “Irish goodbye”. author: John Gruber
description:
Juli Clover, MacRumors:

Apple today added a new option for unlocking the iPhone Duo using the front-facing camera, giving device users multiple ways to access their content. The feature is available in the second iOS 27.3 beta.

The option to unlock with facial recognition is only available on the Lock Screen, and authentication via Touch ID is still needed for Apple Pay purchases, adding passwords and logins, and more. Unlocking with the camera requires a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, and Touch ID is required again after about 45 minutes of inactivity.

This is a much-needed compromise for the lack of Face ID. Good to see Apple adapting quickly to real-world feedback.

There’s also another new Duo feature in 27.3 beta 2: Settings → Display & Brightness → Close to Lock. Turn that on and the Duo locks when you fold it — like, as I wrote in my review
title: ‘Unlock With Front Camera’ — New Feature for iPhone Duo in iOS 27.3 Beta 2

author: John Gruber
description:
Ben Thompson at Stratechery:

This led to what I termed Nvidia’s Risky Business: Nvidia increasingly used its cash flow and credit rating to backstop and fund the companies who were buying its chips. Bears called this circular financing; bulls called it a necessary bridge to a future where AI revenue paid down these companies’ debt and drove massive upside. What is undoubtedly true is that this was the sort of risky business that is uniquely possible for a multi-trillion dollar company that is completely controlled by one man, who has made an entire career of pushing the limits and making risky bets — and seeing them pay off.

author: John Gruber
description:
Robbie Whelan, Anissa Gardizy, Kate Clark, reporting for The Wall Street Journal:

In his final months as chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang was laying the groundwork to pull back the company’s approach to backstopping the AI economy.

Now, with a finance chief at the helm who was already wary of some deals the ousted chief forged, the startups who had been counting on Nvidia’s support expect an even greater pullback.

Just last month, the CEOs of emerging cloud companies that buy Nvidia chips and rent out computing power gathered in Berlin for Nvidia’s premier European artificial-intelligence conference. In a talk that surprised some, Huang’s message was clear: Nvidia’s days as an open checkbook were over.

title: WSJ: ‘Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered’

author: John Gruber
description:
The Oprah Podcast:

In a special holiday episode Oprah brings back one of her legendary traditions with a live audience: ‘Oprah’s Favorite Things!’ Celebrating the 30th anniversary of the iconic list, Oprah surprises an unsuspecting audience full of caregivers with her must-have gifts for the season. From nurses, hospice workers, EMT’s, firefighters to parents caring for a child with special needs Oprah honors their stories and the compassion they show to others every day.

Skip to the end, 1h:02m, for the Duos. The crowd goes bananas.

 ★
title: Oprah Gives Everyone in Her Audience a ‘Duo iPhone’
